root_cause.text: In ath12k, converting management TX handling to `wiphy_work` introduced a lock-ordering bug in `ath12k_mac_op_flush()` where the flush path held the wiphy lock and waited for management-frame completion without first flushing queued `ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work` when `vif == NULL`, so the required work could never run and deadlocked.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that after commit `56dcbf0b5207` the management transmission work became `wiphy_work`, which "can only run under wiphy lock protection," and describes the deadlock scenario where `ath12k_mac_op_flush()` waits in `ath12k_mac_flush()` while holding the wiphy lock; the patch fixes this by moving `for_each_ar(... ) wiphy_work_flush(hw->wiphy, &ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work);` before the `if (!vif)` branch, explicitly noting the old code "does not protect the case where vif being NULL."

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure flush() drains pending management TX work on all radios before proceeding.
intent_record.what: A new loop was added in ath12k_mac_op_flush() before the existing vif NULL check: it iterates over each radio with for_each_ar(ah, ar, i) and calls wiphy_work_flush(hw->wiphy, &ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work) for each one.
intent_record.how: At runtime, flush() now explicitly waits for all pending wmi_mgmt_tx_work items on every radio to complete before continuing, which prevents management transmit work from remaining queued or running past the flush point.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove global wmi_mgmt_tx_work flushing from ath12k_mac_op_flush() so the function only performs its remaining per-vif link flush handling.
intent_record.what: The change removes a three-line loop from ath12k_mac_op_flush() that iterated over each radio context with for_each_ar(ah, ar, i) and called wiphy_work_flush(hw->wiphy, &ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work) before obtaining ahvif and processing vif links.
intent_record.how: At runtime, ath12k_mac_op_flush() no longer forcibly flushes each ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work item for all radios when this flush path is entered. This changes flush behavior by avoiding that management TX work synchronization step here, so the function proceeds directly to per-vif link handling instead of globally waiting for those queued work items.

Remove global wmi_mgmt_tx_work flushing from ath12k_mac_op_flush() so the function only performs its remaining per-vif link flush handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the deadlock root cause by making flush() drain pending management TX work on all radios before waiting, which is exactly what was missing when vif == NULL under the wiphy lock.

The vulnerability is specifically caused by flushing/waiting in ath12k_mac_op_flush() without correctly handling wmi_mgmt_tx_work, leading to deadlock. This change directly modifies that exact flush behavior by removing the global wmi_mgmt_tx_work handling from ath12k_mac_op_flush(), which is part of addressing the lock-ordering/deadlock root cause.

candidates.rationale: When vif == NULL, this early return causes ath12k_mac_op_flush() to skip flushing pending ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work entirely, so later waiting for management TX completion can deadlock because the required work cannot run under the held wiphy lock.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early return in ath12k_mac_op_flush() causes the function to exit when vif == NULL before flushing pending management TX work. Because the flush path holds the wiphy lock and then waits for management-frame completion, skipping the required wmi_mgmt_tx_work flush prevents that work from running and creates the deadlock described in the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code is sufficient because it includes the full flush callback logic relevant to the deadlock condition. In this commit, `ath12k_mac_op_flush()` simply does: `if (drop) return;` and then calls `ath12k_mac_flush(ar);`. The helper `ath12k_mac_flush()` only waits for pending TX to drain using `wait_event_timeout(ar->dp.tx_empty_waitq, (atomic_read(&ar->dp.num_tx_pending) == 0), ATH12K_FLUSH_TIMEOUT);` and logs a warning on timeout. There is no handling to flush queued management TX work such as `ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work` before waiting, and no special handling for the `vif == NULL` case described in the root cause. Because the vulnerable condition is precisely 'flush waits for management-frame completion without first flushing queued work when vif == NULL', and this function contains only the wait path with no prior work flush, the vulnerable construct is present. Therefore this commit has the bug and does not yet contain the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function body `ath12k_mac_op_flush()` is present in full, so the snippet is sufficient. In this commit, `ath12k_mac_op_flush()` only waits for the data-path pending TX count: `wait_event_timeout(ar->dp.tx_empty_waitq, (atomic_read(&ar->dp.num_tx_pending) == 0), ATH12K_FLUSH_TIMEOUT);` and then warns on timeout. It does not reference management TX completion state, does not wait on `num_pending_mgmt_tx`, and does not flush `ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work` or `ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_queue` at all. The root-cause bug described requires a flush path that holds the wiphy lock and waits for management-frame completion without first flushing queued `ar->wmi_mgmt_tx_work` when `vif == NULL`. That vulnerable construct is absent here because this function contains no management-TX flush/wait logic whatsoever. At the same time, the later fix is also not present: there is no handling of `vif == NULL`, no flushing/canceling of `wmi_mgmt_tx_work` inside `ath12k_mac_op_flush()`, and no management TX completion handling before waiting. Therefore `has_bug` is false (the vulnerable construct is absent in this version of the function), and `is_fixed` is false (the eventual fix logic is also absent).
